newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to spend $4.0 bln on military upgrading.
newsitem.headline: Romania to spend $4.0 bln on military upgrading.

text.p: Romania will spend $4.0 billion in the next five years to bring its military hardware up to NATO standards, upgrading fighters and buying electronic warfare equipment, a senior government official said on Monday.
"We have 19 programmes up and running," General Dan Zaharia, secretary of state and head of the army's procurement department, told a news conference.
Romania plans to bring its defence capability close to Western standards and make its equipment compatible with that used by the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
It hopes to be among the first ex-communist states to be incorporated into an expanded NATO later this year, but is generally viewed as an outsider behind Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic.
Zaharia said the planned $4 billion expenditure would come from the state budget and foreign credits, without elaborating.
"We have made the most significant steps of all countries (within the defunct Warsaw Pact) to bring our technology in line with NATO," he said.

Top priorities this year, he said, were a $400 million project with Israel's Elbit Ltd aerospace group to modernise 100-odd Soviet-made MiG-21 fighter jets and 24 French Puma 330 helicopters, manufactured in Romania under licence.
The first batch of 34 upgraded MiG-21s would become operational later this year, Zaharia said.
Purchases of electronic warfare equipment were also planned, but he declined to identify the suppliers.

Talks with the U.S. Bell Helicopter Textron Inc on a $1.0 billion project to coproduce Cobra attack helicopters in Romania were at an advanced stage, he said. Army sources said the contract would be signed in May, ahead of a NATO summit in Madrid where new members are due to be announced.
Projects or talks were also under way with several Western leading military hardware manufacturers to upgrade tanks, army communications and radar systems, Zaharia said.
